problem_understanding: Under load and network issues, writes sometimes disappear, reads become inconsistent, and retries after errors add confusion, suggesting transactional guarantees are weaker than expected.
similar_practical_context: MongoDB 4.2.6 Jepsen analysis: transactional anomalies, weak defaults, and snapshot-isolation gaps.
first_check: Inspect the effective read concern and write concern attached to each transaction in the failing path, instead of relying on client, database, or collection defaults.

result_interpretation.supports_primary_if: If the transaction logs show that read/write concerns are not set per transaction (i.e., defaults are used), confirming that weak defaults are the root cause.
result_interpretation.supports_competing_if: If concerns are set explicitly yet anomalies persist, or if anomalies occur even when no network faults or retries are present, the weaker isolation level hypothesis remains viable.

competing_interpretation: Anomalies may stem from weaker-than-expected isolation semantics that manifest even without network faults.
